reason: E1 directly supports the first three premises by showing that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves ductility while maintaining strength. However, E1 starts from a two-phase B2+BCC alloy, not a single-phase B2 alloy, so the claim that a heat treatment can transform a single-phase B2 into the inverted structure is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Refractory HEAs with continuous B2 matrix and discrete BCC precipitates have poor ductility
Inverting the microstructure to a continuous BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates improves room-temperature ductility
The inverted microstructure maintains high yield strength at room and elevated temperature
The proposed heat treatment can transform a single-phase B2 alloy into the inverted BCC+B2 microstructure
